answer: Each identity posts a 70-credit bond, forges one trellis gate at a harbor forge, and installs the gate at a harbor berth, paying a berth fee that rises with gates. A harbor inspector verifies gate, key, and berth on the board and burns the bond for a missing or reused gate. The first gate costs 36 credits; the kth costs 36+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7029 and 1000 fake identities pay 3,532,500 plus 70,000 locked bonds. A rented-gate ring fails because its gate is already installed, and a second claim burns both bonds. An honest smith pays 36 once and keeps the bond after a clean epoch.
